transcript.text: To help narrow this down, I need to know if the problem is just in the fridge section or both. Is the freezer compartment still cold (around -18°C), or is it also warming up? If the freezer is fine but the fridge is warm, it’s often a blocked air vent or a fan issue; if both are warm, it could be a thermostat setting or a cooling system fault.
freezer still cold, freezes food solid. just the fridge is warm

This is most commonly caused by blocked vents (food pressing against them) or a faulty evaporator fan that circulates the air. Please check two things: 1. Are the air vents (usually on the back wall inside the fridge section) blocked by food or containers? 2. With the door closed, can you hear a faint humming or buzzing sound from inside the fridge compartment (the evaporator fan running)? If it is silent and the vents are clear, please let me know if there is any visible ice build-up at the back of the freezer section.
moved food away from back, no difference. hardly any cold air from the slots. can hear a faint scraping/ticking from the freezer sometimes. theres thick frost on the back wall of the freezer too

The thick frost on the freezer back wall combined with that scraping noise strongly suggests your automatic defrost system has stopped working. The ice is building up over the cooling coils (which makes the freezer stay cold) but also blocking the fan or air vents, so no cold air reaches the fridge section. To identify the specific part you need to replace (usually a heater element or a thermal fuse), I need your make and model number. It is usually on a sticker inside the fridge compartment—often near the salad drawer or on the side wall. Can you read that for me?
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
